Retrieve an indicator as tidy observations

Source: R/indicators.R
knbs_get_indicator.Rd

Returns one row per observation, in one schema whichever source serves the indicator: a census table, a consumer price series, a Data Portal dataflow, a republished dataset or a DHS Program survey indicator.

Usage

knbs_get_indicator(
  indicator,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  geo_level = NULL,
  geo_code = NULL,
  frequency = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  cache = knbs_option("cache"),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

indicator

An indicator id (see knbs_indicators()), or enough of an indicator name to identify one unambiguously.

start, end

Keep only observations in this period range. A year, a "YYYY-MM" month, or a date.

geo_level

Keep only these levels. Census tables: "national", "county", "subcounty". CPI series: "national", "region". DHS Program indicators: "national", "region", "county".

geo_code

Keep only these codes, as character, in the indicator's own geography.

frequency

Keep only series of this frequency: "annual", "quarterly" or "monthly". Only the Open Data for Africa source accepts it — its datasets may carry annual and sub-annual series side by side, and a mixed dataset asks you to choose rather than picking one silently.

source

Source id, to disambiguate an indicator served by more than one source.

cache

Whether to use the local cache.

refresh

Whether to bypass any cached response.

Value

A knbs_indicator tibble. knbs_metadata() returns its provenance; knbs_cite() cites it.

Details

The period convention follows the source's own frequency. Monthly series (the CPI family) carry period as a Date at the first of the month plus a period_label like "2026-06"; census tables carry the census year as an integer period. start and end accept a year (2020), a month ("2020-01"), or a full date, and apply to both conventions.

Geography differs by family and the two systems must not be mixed. Census tables use territory codes (geo_level of "national", "county", "subcounty") that join knbs_geographies(). The CPI series use the CPI collection strata (geo_level of "national" or "region": the Nairobi income bands, Rest of Urban, and the former provinces) — their codes are the source's own and must never be joined against census territories. Six listed CPI regions, the former provinces, carry no data in any period; asking for them returns zero rows because that is the source's answer.

For the CPI family the default is the national series; ask for geo_level = "region" or name geo_codes for more. The CPI portal states no licence and no index base period; knbs_metadata() on the result says so. If the CPI Explorer is down, the error names the KNBS Data Portal series that stands in for the one asked for, and how closely: the portal's index has matched it, its rounded inflation rates have not always.

DHS Program indicators (source = "dhs_program") come with a row for every survey that measured them, 1989 to 2022, with period the survey year and survey naming it ("2022 DHS", "2020 MIS"). characteristic_type and characteristic say which group a value describes: the "Total", a background characteristic such as "Wealth quintile" or "Residence" (for Kenya as a whole), or a "Region". Region rows are the former provinces, or malaria zones, at geo_level "region" with no code; from 2014 the 47 counties are geo_level "county" with 2019 census codes, so they join the census tables. Where the DHS Program gives a value for more than one reference period, every value is kept and preferred marks the one it prefers: keep preferred rows for one value per survey and group.

Every other dimension of a table becomes a pair of columns, <name> holding the source's labels and <name>_code its codes, the way geo_name and geo_code pair up. Census tables use short curated names (marital_status, age, religion, ...); Data Portal flows use their SDMX dimension id in lower case (na_indic, commodity); Open Data for Africa datasets use the portal's dimension id (table, indicator). A Sex dimension is always sex, in lower case. The census age table mixes single years with five-year groups, so it carries age_type ("total", "single_year", "age_group", "other"): keep one type before summing.

See also

knbs_indicators(), knbs_geographies()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cpi <- knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", start = "2020-01")
inflation <- knbs_get_indicator("CPI_INFLATION_YOY", geo_level = "region")
pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc") # Gross County Product
stunting <- knbs_get_indicator("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", geo_level = "county") # KDHS
} # }
